items.title: Sleeping Beauties: David Byrne on Why Transformative Ideas Fall Dormant and How They Awaken to Change the World
items.description: Each time you look up at the night sky, you see only ancient signals — by the time a photon has reached your pupil, the star that emitted it may be long dead. The great wonder is that its light can traverse immense expanses of space and time to gladden the darkness of today, to cast wonder upon this lonely planet. An idea is a signal that may travel across immense expanses of space and time before it touches the world. Transformative ideas can and often do fall on the closed eyes of their epoch.

items.title: Vincent van Gogh on Fear, Taking Risks, and How Inspired Mistakes Propel Us Forward
items.description: "However meaningless and vain, however dead life appears, the man of faith, of energy, of warmth... steps in and does something."

items.title: But We Had Music: Nick Cave Reads an Animated Poem about How to Be More Alive
items.description: How, knowing that even the universe is dying, do we bear our lives? Most readily, through friendship, through connection, through co-creating the world we want to live in for the brief time we have together on this lonely, perfect planet. items.title: The Importance of Being Scared: Polish Nobel Laureate Wisława Szymborska on Fairy Tales and the Necessity of Fear
items.description: "Andersen had the courage to write stories with unhappy endings. He didn’t believe that you should try to be good because it pays ... but because evil stems from intellectual and emotional stuntedness and is the one form of poverty that should be shunned."

items.title: A Constellation of Amazements: An Illustrated Love Letter to the Joy of Collecting Things
items.description: We are hunter-gatherers with a capacity for amazement, wired to search for an organizing principle by which to contain the chaos of reality. We organize what we find into categories and hierarchies, hovering over which is one of the strangest things about being human: preference. How odd to have a strong feeling about a color or an object or a sequence of chords. And yet our preferences are how we sculpt the self from the monolith of the species. items.title: How to Remake Yourself When You Are Undone: Lincoln and the Gift of His Suicidal Depression
items.description: Life-affirming inspiration from a man who knew intimately “that intensity of thought, which will some times wear the sweetest idea thread-bare and turn it to the bitterness of death.”

items.title: Nietzsche on Walking and Creativity
items.description: "Our first questions about the value of a book, of a human being, or a musical composition are: Can they walk? Even more, can they dance?"

items.title: Dostoyevsky on What Makes a Good Person
items.description: We know good people when we encounter them, when they fall upon our lives like a sunbeam, like a song. But we don’t always know what makes them good. It has, of course, a lot to do with kindness. It has to do with their capacity to give, and also to receive. It has to do with their courage of uncertainty.
